source_text: Ἐὰν δὲ φαγὼν φάγῃ ἀπὸ τῶν κρεῶν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ, οὐ δεχθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ προσφέροντι αὐτὸ, οὐ λογισθήσεται αὐτῷ, μίασμά ἐστιν· ἡ δὲ ψυχὴ ἤτις ἂν φάγῃ ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, μιανθήσεται, καὶ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν λήψεται.» Τριταῖον μὲν οὖν ἀποπέμπεται θῦμα, παραιτεῖται δὲ ὅτι καὶ τὸ χθιζὸν, διεσάφει λέγων. «Ἐὰν δὲ θύσῃς θυσίαν εὐχὴν χαρμοσύνης τῷ Κυρίῳ, εἰς δεκτὸν ὑμῖν θύσετε αὐτό. Αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ βρωθήσεται, οὐ καταλείψεται ἀπὸ τῶν κρεῶν εἰς τὸ πρωΐ· ἐγώ εἰμι Κύριος· τὴν ἁμαρτίαν λήψεται.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εἶτα τίς ἂν γένοιτο καὶ τῶνδε ὁ νοῦς; {ΚΥΡ.} Προαποδέδειχεν ἡμῖν ὁ νόμος ἐν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω πλειστάκις, ὅτι τὸν ἅπαντα χρόνον κατατέμνειν ἔθος τῇ θείᾳ Γραφῇ, ποτὲ μὲν εἰς δύο, καθ' ὃν ἦν ὁ νόμος, καὶ καθ' ὃν ἐπέλαμψεν ὁ Χριστός· ποτὲ δὲ αὖ, εἰς τρεῖς παρεισκρινομένου τε καὶ τὰ τάττοντος μεταξὺ, καὶ καθ' ὃν ὁ τῶν ἁγίων προφητῶν ἀνέλαμψε χορὸς, πλὴν ὅτι καὶ ἐν χρόνῳ τῷ κατὰ Μωσέα, καὶ ἐν τῷ τῶν ἁγίων προφητῶν λατρείας ἦν τρόπος ὁ αὐτὸς, ὡς ἐν σκιαῖς ἔτι ταῖς κατὰ νόμον. Πρωΐας δὲ γενομένης, ἤτοι τοῦ τρίτου λοιπὸν πάλιν ἀναδειχθέντος καιροῦ, καὶ τοῦ νοητοῦ φωτὸς, τοῦτ' ἔστι, Χριστοῦ, τὴν ὑφ' ἥλιον περιαστράπτοντος, λελυμένης δὲ λοιπὸν τῆς παλαιᾶς ἀχλύος, οὐκέτι δεκτὸς τῆς τὸ τηνικάδε λατρείας ὁ τρόπος, ἀλλ' εἴτε χθιζὸν, εἴτ' οὖν εἴη τὸ τριταῖον στέαρ, ἢ θύμα, δεκτὸν μὲν οὐκέτι, βδελυρὸν δὲ καὶ ἀπόβλητον παρὰ Θεῷ, καὶ ἐν μιάσματος τάξει λελογισμένον τοῖς οὐκ ἐν καιρῷ προσκομίζειν ᾑρημένοις. Ἢ οὐκ εἶναι φὴς ἀληθὲς, ὅτι Χριστοῦ καταλάμποντος τοῖς εὐαγγελικοῖς παιδεύμασι τὰς τῶν ἁγίων ψυχὰς καὶ εἰς λατρείαν τὴν πνευματικὴν μυσταγωγοῦντος εὖ μάλα, περιττά πως ἤδη καὶ ἀνωφελῆ τὰ ἐν νόμῳ; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Φημί. Μεμνήσομαι γὰρ τοῦ θεσπεσίου Παύλου, σκύβαλα καὶ ζημίαν ἀποκεκληκότος τὰ κατὰ νόμον αὐχήματα, διὰ τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Ἀκούω δὲ γεγραφότος τισί· «Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν περιτέμνησθε, Χριστὸς οὐδὲν ἡμᾶς ὠφελήσει.» {ΚΥΡ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. Οὐκοῦν ἁμαρτία καὶ μολυσμὸς, ἀναδειχθέντος Χριστοῦ, καὶ παρελάσαντος τοῦ καιροῦ, καθ' ὃν ἦν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται, τῆς ὡς ἐν σκιαῖς λατρείας ἀντέχεσθαι· καὶ Θεῷ προσάγειν ἐπιχειρεῖν ὄϊν, ἢ στέαρ, ἢ λιβανωτόν· καίτοι λέγοντος ἐναργῶς τοῦ Υἱοῦ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί· «Θυσίαν καὶ προσφορὰν οὐκ ἠθέλησας, σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι. Ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ ηὐδόκησας, τότε εἶπον, Ἰδοὺ ἥκω· ἐν κεφαλίδι βιβλίου γέγραπται περὶ ἐμοῦ, τοῦ ποιῆσαι, ὁ Θεὸς, τὸ θέλημά σου.» Ἄμωμον γὰρ ὥσπερ ἱερεῖον ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀναθεὶς ὁ Υἱὸς, ἔστησε τὰ ἐν νόμῳ, περιελεῖν ἁμαρτίας οὐ δυνάμενα· τέλος γὰρ νόμου καὶ προφητῶν ὁ Χριστός. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης.
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing Lev 7:18 LXX:] If eating he eats of the meats on the third day, it will not be accepted (δέχομαι) for him who offers it, it will not be reckoned (λογίζομαι) to him; it is a defilement (μίασμα); and the soul which eats of it will be defiled (μιαίνω) and will take (λαμβάνω) the sin (ἁμαρτία). So the third-day (τριταῖον) victim is sent away (ἀποπέμπω); and that he refuses (παραιτέομαι) also yesterday's (χθιζόν), he made clear saying [Lev 22:29-30 LXX + Lev 19:8 tail]: if you sacrifice a sacrifice, a vow of rejoicing (εὐχὴ χαρμοσύνης) to the Lord, into acceptance (εἰς δεκτόν) for you you shall sacrifice it; on that same day it shall be eaten; there shall not be left of the meats into the morning (πρωΐ); I am the Lord; he will take the sin. PALL: Then what would be the sense (νοῦς) of these also? CYR: The law has shown beforehand (προαποδείκνυμι) to us in the things above very often that it is the custom (ἔθος) of the divine Scripture (θεία Γραφή) to cut up (κατατέμνω) all time, sometimes into two, that in which the law was and that in which Christ shone upon (ἐπιλάμπω); sometimes again into three, [a time] being inserted (παρεισκρίνω) and set (τάσσω) between, the one in which the choir (χορός) of the holy prophets shone out (ἀναλάμπω); except that both in the time of Moses and in that of the holy prophets the manner (τρόπος) of worship (λατρεία) was the same, as still in the shadows (σκιαί) according to law. But morning having come, that is, the third time (καιρός) having at last been shown forth, and the intelligible light (νοητὸν φῶς), that is Christ, flashing around (περιαστράπτω) the [earth] under the sun, and the old mist (ἀχλύς) having been dissolved (λύω), the manner of the worship of that time is no longer acceptable (δεκτός); but whether yesterday's or third-day fat or victim, it is no longer acceptable but loathsome (βδελυρός) and rejected (ἀπόβλητος) with God, and reckoned in the rank of defilement for those choosing to bring it not in season (οὐκ ἐν καιρῷ). Or do you say it is not true that, Christ illumining with gospel teachings (εὐαγγελικὰ παιδεύματα) the souls of the saints and initiating (μυσταγωγέω) very well into spiritual worship (λατρεία πνευματική), the things in law are somehow already superfluous (περιττά) and unprofitable (ἀνωφελῆ)? PALL: I say [so]. For I shall remember the divine Paul, who called the boasts (αὐχήματα) according to law dung / refuse (σκύβαλα) and loss (ζημία), because of the surpassing (τὸ ὑπερέχον) of the knowledge of Christ. And I hear him having written to some: 'I say to you that if you are circumcised (περιτέμνω), Christ will profit us [read you] nothing.' CYR: Rightly said. So it is sin and pollution (μολυσμός), Christ having been shown forth and the time having passed by (παρελαύνω) in which were the law and the prophets, to hold to (ἀντέχομαι) the worship as in shadows, and to attempt to bring to God sheep (ὄϊς) or fat or frankincense (λιβανωτός); although the Son says clearly (ἐναργῶς) to the God and Father: [Heb 10:5-7 = LXX Ps 39:7-9] sacrifice and offering (προσφορά) you did not will, but a body (σῶμα) you prepared (καταρτίζω) for me; whole burnt offerings and [offerings] for sin you were not pleased with (εὐδοκέω); then I said: behold, I come; in the roll (κεφαλίς) of the book it is written about me, to do, O God, your will (θέλημα). For the Son, having dedicated (ἀνατίθημι) himself for us as a blameless (ἄμωμος) victim (ἱερεῖον), stopped (ἵστημι) the things in law, unable to take away (περιαιρέω) sins; for the end (τέλος) of law and prophets is Christ. PALL: Well said.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …But if he does eat any of the flesh on the third day, it shall not be accepted for the one who offers it; it shall not be credited to him; it is a defilement; and the soul that eats of it shall be defiled and shall bear the sin’ (Leviticus 7:18). So the sacrifice of the third day is rejected; and that yesterday’s is refused as well, he made plain by saying: ‘If you sacrifice to the Lord a sacrifice, a vow of rejoicing, you shall sacrifice it so that it is acceptable for you. On that same day it shall be eaten; none of the flesh shall be left until morning; I am the Lord’ (Leviticus 22:29–30); ‘he shall bear the sin’ (Leviticus 19:8).
Palladius: Then what might be the meaning of these as well?

Cyril: The law has shown us many times already in what came before that divine Scripture is accustomed to divide the whole of time sometimes into two: the time when the law was in force, and the time when Christ shone forth; and sometimes again into three, inserting and placing between them the time when the choir of the holy prophets shone forth; except that in the time of Moses and in that of the holy prophets the manner of worship was the same, since it was still in the shadows of the law. But when morning has come, that is, when the third season has at last been revealed in turn, and the spiritual light, that is, Christ, shines all around the world beneath the sun, and the ancient mist has at last been dispersed, the manner of worship of that former time is no longer acceptable. Whether the fat or the sacrifice is yesterday’s or the third day’s, it is no longer acceptable, but loathsome and rejected before God, and counted as a defilement for those who choose to bring it out of season. Or would you not say it is true that, now that Christ illumines the souls of the saints with the teachings of the Gospel and initiates them so well into spiritual worship, the things in the law have somehow become superfluous and useless?

Palladius: I would. For I will call to mind the inspired Paul, who called the law’s grounds for boasting refuse and loss because of the surpassing worth of the knowledge of Christ (Philippians 3:7–8). And I hear him writing to some: ‘I tell you that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing’ (Galatians 5:2).

Cyril: You are right. So it is sin and defilement, now that Christ has been revealed and the time of the law and the prophets has gone by, to cling to worship as in shadows, and to attempt to bring to God a sheep, or fat, or frankincense, even though the Son says plainly to God the Father: ‘Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but a body you have prepared for me; in burnt offerings and sin offerings you took no pleasure. Then I said: See, I have come, as it is written of me in the scroll of the book, to do your will, O God’ (Hebrews 10:5–7; Psalm 40:6–8). For the Son, offering himself up for us as a spotless victim (Hebrews 9:14), put a stop to the things of the law, which could not take away sins (Hebrews 10:11); for Christ is the end of the law and the prophets (Romans 10:4).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-quotation, completing Leviticus 7:16-18 from section 25; Migne adds μιανθήσεται ('shall be defiled') to LXX 7:18, kept. The second quotation is Leviticus 22:29-30 LXX (εὐχὴν χαρμοσύνης, 'a vow of rejoicing'); its last clause, τὴν ἁμαρτίαν λήψεται, is not in 22:30 and matches Leviticus 19:8 (also 7:18), so it is cited separately; the old English's Leviticus 19:5-8 for the whole quotation was wrong. Προαποδέδειχεν ἡμῖν ὁ νόμος: Migne reads 'the law' (ὁ νόμος); with ἐν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω ('in what came before') it may be a misprint for ὁ λόγος ('our discussion'); translated as printed. καὶ τὰ τάττοντος μεταξὺ is corrupt in Migne; sense taken as a third period inserted between. The time-scheme: 'morning' stands for Christ's coming, the third period after the law and the prophets; any legal offering kept over, 'yesterday's' or 'the third day's', is no longer acceptable. Cyril's present tenses are kept. Galatians 5:2: Migne prints ἡμᾶς ('us'), an itacistic slip for NT ὑμᾶς; rendered 'you'. Philippians 3:7-8 supplies σκύβαλα, ζημία and τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως. The Son's words match Hebrews 10:5-7 verbatim (σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι, οὐκ ηὐδόκησας); LXX Psalm 39:7-9 = English Psalm 40:6-8 (renumbered). 'Spotless victim' alludes to Hebrews 9:14 (ἑαυτὸν προσήνεγκεν ἄμωμον); 'could not take away sins' reproduces Hebrews 10:11 (περιελεῖν ἁμαρτίας). Romans 10:4 has 'end of the law'; Cyril adds 'and the prophets'. The 'shadows' of the law echo Hebrews 10:1 and 'the time of the law and the prophets' echoes Luke 16:16 / Matthew 11:13; both general, left uncited.
